en: Jose Rizal secretly used the pseudonym Dimasalang to avoid Spanish authorities while writing his famous anti-colonial novels.
Marcela Agoncillo and her daughter sewed the first official Philippine flag in Hong Kong before it was unfurled in Kawit.
The President of the Philippines is limited to a single six-year term and is strictly prohibited from running for re-election.
The Philippine eagle, our national bird, is one of the largest in the world with a wingspan reaching two meters.
The MassKara Festival in Bacolod features dancers wearing massive, smiling masks to celebrate the city's resilience during a 1980s sugar crisis.
The Ifugao people carved the magnificent Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over two thousand years ago using only simple hand tools.
Baybayin, the ancient pre-colonial Filipino writing system, uses exactly seventeen basic symbols consisting of three vowels and fourteen consonants.
The Filipino value of bayanihan originated from the physical act of an entire community carrying a traditional nipa hut to a new location.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented an improvised bamboo incubator to help care for premature babies in rural Philippine hospitals without electricity.
Julian Felipe composed the original instrumental melody of the Philippine national anthem in just one single day.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution explicitly guarantees every citizen's fundamental right to a balanced and healthful ecology in harmony with nature.
Although the Philippines is an archipelago of over 7,600 islands, only about 2,000 of these islands are actually inhabited by people.
